title: ChIP-seq analysis of histone modifications and CCCTC-binding factor (CTCF) binding in the livers of five strains of mouse and rat
design_description: ChIP-seq analysis of histone modifications and CCCTC-binding factor (CTCF) binding in the livers of five strains of mouse and rat
protocol: Livers from males were perfused in situ with PBS and then dissected, minced, cross-linked using 1% formaldehyde solution for 20 min, quenched for 10 min with 250 mM glycine, washed twice with ice-cold PBS, and tissue pellets were stored at -80°C. Livers (ten livers pooled for mouse or one liver for rat) were homogenised, washed twice with PBS, and lysed according to published protocols (Schmidt et al. 2009). Chromatin was sonicated to an average fragment length of 300 bp. Chromatin was immunoprecipitated using either 10 μl H3K4me3 antibody (mouse monoclonal, Merck Millipore 05-1339, lot 2780484); 10 μl H3K27ac antibody (rabbit polyclonal, AbCam 4729, lot GR3187598-1); 20 μl CTCF antibody (rabbit polyclonal, Merck Millipore 07-729, lot 2517762). Immunoprecipitated DNA or input DNA (max 50 ng) was used for library preparation using the ThruPLEX DNA-Seq library preparation protocol (Rubicon Genomics, UK) as described previously (Aitken et al. 2018). Library fragment size was determined using a 2100 Bioanalyzer (Agilent).

design_description: Dysregulated DNA Methylation in Abca4-/- Retinal Pigment Epithelium: Insights into Early Stage of Stargardt Disease
protocol: Mice were euthanized by cervical dislocation, and eyes were harvested for obtaining RPE/eyecup separated from neural retina. In 1x phosphate buffer saline (PBS, pH 7.4), the anterior segment of the eye was removed, followed by the separation of the neural retina from the eyecup. RPE/Eyecups were stored in a −80 °C freezer until further processing. DNA was extracted from mice, one RPE/eyecup per sample, using the Dneasy Blood & Tissue Kit (Qiagen, Hilden, Germany, Cat# 69506). DNA was eluted in 50 μL AE Buffer. The concentration was measured with a Qubit instrument (Life Technologies, Carlsbad, CA, USA), and 100 ng of genomic DNA was treated with RNAse enzyme at 37 °C for 30 min to remove contaminating RNA. RRBS libraries were prepared by a Zymo-Seq RRBS Library kit (Zymo research, Irvine, CA, USA, Cat# D5460). The libraries were subjected to size selection using magnetic AMPure XP beads (Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, Indianapolis, IN, USA) to enrich DNA fragments of the desired size. The quality control of the final libraries (size-selected and barcoded) was performed using an Agilent TapStation 4200 (D1000, D5000; Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA, USA).

title: GSM7806252: parn1_prg1D654A_rep1; Caenorhabditis elegans; miRNA-Seq
protocol: 60,000 L1 larvae were plated to 150 mm NGM plates supplemented with 2 mL of concentrated OP50 food. Approximately 64 hours after plating L1 larvae, day 1 adults with eggs were collected from plates using M9 solution. Harvested animals were washed twice with M9 and once with water. Animals were then suspended in TRI Reagent solution (Sigma) and frozen at -80°C until RNA extraction was performed. To extract RNAs animals suspended in TRI Reagent solution were thawed and lysed using a Bead Mill (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Bromo-chloropropane (Sigma) was added to the lysed worms and centrifuged at 12,000 x g for 15 minutes. Following centrifugation, the aqueous phase was pipetted to an equal volume of cold isopropanol and placed at -20°C for 1 hour to precipitate RNAs. RNAs were pelleted by centrifugation at 20,000 x g for 15 minutes at 4°C. Total RNAs were washed with 75% EtOH twice and suspended in RNAse free water. Small RNAs were enriched from total RNAs using the MirVana miRNA isolation kit according (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Small RNAs were treated with RNA phosphatase PIR-1 to remove gamma and beta phosphates from the 5' triphosphorylated RNAs (50). Monophosphorylated RNAs were ligated to 3' adapters ( rAppAGATCGGAAGAGCACACGTCTGAACTCCAGTCA/3ddC/, IDT) using T4 RNA ligase 2 in 25% PEG 8000 (NEB) at 15 C overnight. A 5' adapter (rArCrArCrUrCrUrUrUrCrCrCrUrArCrArCrGrArCrGrCrUrCrUrUrCrCrGrArUrCrU, IDT) was then ligated to RNAs to the product using T4 RNA ligase 1 (NEB) for 4 hours at 15 C. Ligated products were reverse transcribed using SuperScript IV Reverse Transcriptase (Thermo Fisher Scientific) to convert RNA to cDNA libraries. cDNA libraries were amplified by PCR and subsequently sequenced on an Illumina Novaseq platform (SP2 x 50 bp) at the OSU Comprehensive Cancer Center genomics core.

title: GSM9004221: MicroC, Day7 Neuron, Aux Day0-7, rep2; Mus musculus; Hi-C
protocol: NPCs and Day 7 In-vitro differentiated neurons were harvested, counted and collected in 10%FCS/1XPBS and double crosslinked using formaldehyde (ThermoFisher #28908) and DSG (disuccinimidyl glutarate, 7.7Å) (TCI, D5445), respectively. Following quenching of the fixation reactions and washes in ice-cold 1xPBS, 5M cell aliquots were pelleted and snap-frozen in liquid nitrogen for storage at −80°C. Cell membranes were solubilized to extract intact nuclei by resuspending crosslinked 5M cell pellets in Micro-C Buffer #1 (MB#1; 50 mM NaCl, 10 mM Tris-HCl pH = 7.5, 5 mM MgCl2, 1M CaCl2, 0.2% NP-40, 1x Protease Inhibitor Cocktail) at 1M cells per 100 μL for 20 min on ice. Following an MB#1 wash, samples were resuspended in 250 μL MB#1 and 1 μL of 20 U/μL MNase (Worthington Biochem #LS004798). The digestion reaction was thoroughly mixed and incubated at 37°C for 15 min on a thermomixer shaking 850rpm. MNase was inactivated by the addition of 200mM EGTA (4 mM final conc.) and incubating for 10 min at 65˚C. at this stage, a digestion efficiency determination step was performed: aliquots of digested and undigested samples were treated with Proteinase K for 1-2 hours at 65˚C, to reverse crosslink. After purification of the the DNA using ZymoClean DNA purification kit, the fragments size was measured on TapeStation, to ensure primarily (~80%) mononucleosomal fragments (150-200 bp). Digested nuclei were washed twice with ice-cold Micro-C Buffer #2 (50 mM NaCl, 10 mM Tris-HCl pH = 7.5, 10 mM MgCl2). To generate blunt ends on digested DNA fragments prior to proximity ligation and add biotinylated nucleotides, a series of enzymatic processing steps were performed. First, for addition of 5'-phosphate groups and removal of 3'-phosphate groups, digested samples were incubated with: 10xNEBuffer 2.1 (NEB, #B7202S), 100mM ATP (NEB, #P0756), 100mM DTT and 10U/μL T4 PNK (NEB, #M0201), at 37°C for 15 min with interval mixing. Then 50 U of DNA Polymerase I Klenow Fragment (NEB #M0210) was added to the reaction and incubated at 37°C for 15 min with interval mixing. Next, the following mixture was added to each sample: 10 mM dGTP and dTTP (NEB, #N0446), 1mM Biotin-dATP and Biotin-dCTP (Jena Bioscience, #NU-835-BIO14, #NU-809-BIOX), T4 DNA Ligase Buffer and BSA. The reactin was incubated for 45 min at 25°C with interval mixing and then quenched by 30 mM EDTA heat inactivate for 20 min at 65°C. Finally, the samples were washed once with cold Micro-C Buffer #3 (50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5, 10 mM MgCl2). Proximity ligation and Removal of unligated ends was performed by first washing the samples with 1x Ligase buffer, followed by resuspending in ligation reaction mix: 10x NEB Ligase buffer, 200xBSA, and 400U/ μl NEB T4 Ligase (NEB, #M0202L) and slowly rotating at RT for 2-3 h. Then, the chromatin was collected and removal of biotinylated dNTPs from all unligated fragment ends was performed by incubating the samples in 10x NEBuffer#1 (NEB # B7001) and 100U/ μl Exonuclease III (NEB # M0206), for 15 min at 37°C with interval mixing. Reverse crosslinking of the samples was performed by incubating with 20mg/ml Proteinase K, 10% SDS and 100mg/ml RNase A overnight at 65°C. After reverse crosslinking, Dinucleosomal DNA was purified in two steps: first, phenol:chloroform:isoamylic alcohol DNA extraction was performed. Then, the samples were loaded on 2% agarose gel. Band between 250 – 400 bp was cut out of the gel and then purified Zymo Gel Purification kit (Zymo Research #D4008). DNA amounts were Measured using Qubit™ High Sensitivity dsDNA kit. The biotin-bound ligated DNA contact fragments were pulled down using Dynabeads MyOne Streptavidin C1 (Invitrogen #65001) in TBW (10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, 1 mM EDTA, 2 M NaCl), and then washed once with 10mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5. For each micro-C sample, libraries were generated using the NEBNext Ultra II DNA Library Prep Kit (NEB, E7645), without size selection and with Pre-PCR wash of the beads with 100 μl 0.1xTE. PCR amplification of libraries was performed with 8 cycles of enrichment. Finally, libraries were purified using 0.9X AmPure XP beads (Beckman Coulter #A63880). Final libraries were quality controlled for size and concentration and sequenced on a NovaSeq Illumina sequencer with 100-bp paired-end reads.

title: GSM9193703: hic_stag1_4h_with_a_rep2; Mus musculus; Hi-C
protocol: FACS purified cells (0.1 million) were lysed in 1ml cold Cell Lysis Buffer (10mM Tris pH 8, 10mM NaCl, 0.2% NP-40/Igepal) for 10min on ice. Nuclei were pelleted at 4℃ and washed once with cold 1.4 × NEB buffer 3.1 (NEB Cat#B7203S). Nuclei were then re-suspended in 25ul of 1.4 × NEB buffer 3.1 and treated with 0.1% SDS for 10min at 65℃. Nuclei were then treated with 1% Triton X-100 to quench SDS for 1h at 37℃. Chromatin was digested with 30U DpnII restriction enzyme (NEB, Cat#R0543M) at 37℃ overnight with shaking (950rpm on a thermal mixer). After overnight digestion, an additional stroke of 30U DpnII was added into the system to further digest the genome for 4 hours at 37℃. After the 2nd stroke of digestion, nuclei were incubated at 65℃ for 20min to inactivate DpnII. Digested chromatin fragments were then cooled down to room temperature and blunted with dCTP, dGTP, dTTP (Diamond Cat#B110049, B110050, B110051) and Biotin-14-dATP (active motif, Catalog No: 14138) using 6.6U DNA Polymerase I, Large (Klenow) fragment (NEB, Cat#M0210). Chromatin was then ligated in-situ with 2000U T4 DNA ligase (NEB, Cat#M0202M) for 4 hours at 16℃ followed by further incubation for 2 hours at room temperature. Chromatin was then reverse-crosslinked overnight at 65℃ in the presence of 1% SDS and proteinase K (G-clone Cat#EZ0970). title: GSM9425029: oocyte,scBS-seq,ctrl04; Mus musculus; Bisulfite-Seq
protocol: The 8-week-old mice were anesthetized by intraperitoneal injection of tribromoethanol (350 mg/kg). Following anesthesia, the mice were first perfused with 0.1 M phosphate-buffered saline (PBS, pH 7.4) to remove blood and interstitial fluids from the tissues. For mice designated for dorsal dentate gyrus (dDG) DNA/RNA extraction, the mice were then rapidly decapitated. Ovulation during natural estrus is commonly achieved induced using hCG doses ranging from 2.5 to 10 IU. To approximate the higher hCG exposure category defined in our discovery cohort (> 6,750 IU on trigger day), we administered a medium-high dose of hCG (7.5 IU) via intraperitoneal injection to female mice in natural estrus to induce ovulation without PMSG pretreatment. In the control group, females in estrus were housed individually with a sterile vasectomized male mouse. The next morning from 8:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m., mice with vaginal plugs or 14 h after hCG injection were euthanized by cervical dislocation. Cumulus-oocyte complexes (COCs) were subsequently collected from the oviductal ampullae. Denuded metaphase II (MII) oocytes were then isolated by removing the cumulus mass using a medium containing 0.5 mg/ml hyaluronidase at 37℃. For blastocyst collection, the optimal timing occurs at 3.5 dpc (embryonic day E3.5), when embryos have reached the fully-formed blastocyst stage and are typically located within the uterine lumen. A 30-gauge Hamilton blunt needle attached to a 1 mL syringe pre-loaded with warm flushing medium is carefully inserted into the uterus at a location close to the utero-tubal junction, the anatomical boundary between the oviduct and uterine horn. The plunger of the syringe is gently depressed to flush approximately 1 mL of medium through the uterine horn, expelling the embryos and uterine fluid into a clean petri dish containing PBS. After oocytes and blastocysts washed three times with 0.1% BSA/PBS, each sample  was then transferred into 0.2 ml PCR tubes containing 2 μl lysis buffer. Transcriptome libraries were prepared following the Smart-seq2 protocol.Total RNA was extracted from dDG tissue samples using the RNeasy Plus Mini Kit (Qiagen, Cat No. 74134) following the manufacturer's protocol. The quantity and quality of the extracted RNA were assessed using a Qubit 4.0 fluorometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and the Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer, respectively. RNA integrity number (RIN) values greater than 7.0 were considered acceptable for sequencing. Sequencing libraries were constructed using the VAHTS Universal V8 RNA-seq Library Prep Kit for Illumina (Vazyme, NR605) according to the manufacturer's instructions. Library preparation was performed by scBS-seq protocol with some modifications. For bisulfite conversion, EZ DNA Methylation-Direct Kit (Zymo Research; D5020) was used. After zona pellucida removal, we collected 16 pools ( ctrl 8, hCG8) of 10 oocytes per group and 16 pools (ctrl 8, hCG8 ) of 10 blastocysts in a single 200 μl tube containing 2.5 μl of Buffer RLT (QIAGEN; 79216). Samples were stored at -80°C. After thawing, 7.5 μl of nuclease-free water and 65 μl of CT conversion reagent (EZ DNA Methylation-Direct Kit; Zymo D5020) were added and samples were incubated in a PCR machine (98°C 8 min, 65°C 180 min). DNA was purified by using MagBinding Beads (Zymo EZ Methylation Direct MagPrep Kit, Zymo, D5044). DNA bound to the MagBinding Beads was washed by M-wash buffer once, 100 μl of M-Desulphonation buffer was applied on the beads and the incubation was done at room temperature for 15 min to complete the CT-conversion. DNA on the beads was further washed twice and then eluted with the DNA strand synthesis with 1x Blue buffer (Enzymatics), 600 nM of dNTPs, 400 nM of P5-N6-oligo1(CTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCTNNNNNN). DNA mixture was denatured at 65°C for 3 min and quickly chilled. Then 1 μl of Klenow Fragment (3'-5' exo-) (Enzymatics; P7010-LC-L) was added and the strand synthesis reaction was done in the PCR machine with the following program (4°C for 5 min, 4°C rising to 37°C with increasing0.1°C every 1 sec, 37°C for 30 min, 4°C pause). Then, the remained oligos and dNTPs were deactivated by Exo-CIP™ Rapid PCR Cleanup Kit (NEB, E1050S) following the manufacture's protocol. Next, dC tailing was conducted in the presence of 1 x Blue buffer (Enzymatics), 2.5 mM of dCTPs and 1U/μL of TdT enzyme. After that, the second strand synthesis was performed by tagging the P7-G6-oligo2 (AGACGTGTGCTCTTCCGATCTGGGGGGHN) in the presence of 1 × Blue buffer (Enzymatics), 600 nM of dNTPs, 400 nM of P7-G6-oligo2 and 100 units of Klenow exo- (Enzymatics) and incubated at 37 °C for 1 h, followed by Agencourt AMPure XP beads (Beckman) purification. Final libraries were generated by 18 cycles of PCR to incorporate universal primers and index primers and purified by Agencourt AMPure XP beads. The libraries were pooled, checked and sequenced with paired-end 150-bp reads on an Illumina NovaSeq6000 platform.For RRBS, each DNA sample was extracted from dDG tissue spiked with 0.5% lambda DNA (Thermo Fisher Scientific, SD0021) and digested with the methylation-insensitive restriction enzyme MspI (NEB, M7634S), followed by end-repair, A-tailing and ligation with methylated adaptors using KAPA HyperPlus Library Preparation Kit (Roche, KK8514). After adaptor ligation, the DNA was subjected to bisulfite treatment using the DNA Methylation-Lightning Kit (Zymo, Cat. No. D5031). The bisulfite-converted DNA was then amplified using KAPA HiFi Uracil + enzyme (Roche, Cat. No. KK2802). The PCR products were purified using the AMPure XP beads at a 0.8:1 ratio (Beckman) to obtain the final RRBS library.

title: GSM9542750: Cdc45-mAID G1-Control Thymidine 15h ESCs Replicate 2, Hi-C; Mus musculus; Hi-C
protocol: Hi-C experiments were performed as previously reported with some modifications (Kadota et al., 2020). Cells were fixed with 1% formaldehyde for 10 min at room temperature. Glycine was added to 0.125 M final concentration and incubated for 5 min at room temperature. Tubes were placed on ice for 15 min. Cells were washed in ice-cold PBS by centrifuging at 400 g at 4°C. Then, 1–2 x 10^6 fixed cell pellets were used for the following steps. Cell pellets were resuspended in 400 µl of lysis buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0), 10 mM NaCl, 0.2% NP-40) with 1x protease inhibitor cocktail (Roche, 11873580001), transferred to 1.5 ml Protein LoBind Tubes (Eppendorf) and incubated on ice for 20 min. The samples were spun down for 5 min at 1000 g at 4℃. After removing the supernatants carefully, pellets were resuspended in 250 µl of 1x NEBuffer 2 with 0.3% SDS and incubated for 1 h at 37°C in the Thermomixer C3 at 1100 rpm (Eppendorf). Then, 28 µl of 20% Triton X-100 were added to 2% final concentration and the samples were incubated for 1 h at 37°C. Next, 100 U of DpnIII (NEB, R0543S) was added and the samples were incubated overnight at 37°C in the Thermomixer C3 at 1100 rpm. The next day, after the inactivation of enzyme activity with 65˚C for 20 min, the samples were spun down for 5 min at 4°C. After removing the supernatants carefully, pellets were resuspended in 100 µl of “Biotin fill-in mix” (1 x NEBuffer 2, 15 µM each of dCTP, dGTP, dTTP and 15 µM of Biotin-14-dATP (Invitrogen, 19524-016), 15 U of Klenow (NEB, M0210S), 1% Triton X-100) and incubated for 45 min at 25°C. After spinning down for 5 min at 4°C and removing the supernatants carefully, the pellets were resuspended in 100 µl of “Ligation Mix” (1x T4 DNA ligase buffer (NEB), 6 µl of T4 DNA ligase (1 U/µl, Invitrogen, 15224-025), 1% Triton X-100) and incubated 6 hours at 16°C. The sample volumes were brought up to ~100 µl by adding 10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0) / 5 mM EDTA and RNaseA-treated for 30 min at 37°C by adding 5 µl of 10 mg/ml RNaseA. Reverse-crosslinking and proteinase K treatment were performed overnight at 65°C by adding ""Reverse-crosslink Mix"" (1.5% SDS, 375 mM NaCl, 1 mg/ml Proteinase K). The next day, 5 µl of 20 mg/ml Proteinase K was added and incubated for 2 h at 55°C. Samples were then extracted twice with phenol/chloroform and once with chloroform. After this, 500 µl of 2-propanol was added. The samples were incubated for 10 min and spun down for 30 min at 20,000 g at 4°C for DNA precipitation. After 70% EtOH washes (add 1 ml, cfg for 5 min at 20,000 g at 4°C), the DNA pellets were resuspended in 30 µl of EB (QIAGEN, 19086). For generating next-generation sequencing libraries, 1-2 µg of Hi-C DNA was used per library. To remove biotin from unligated ends, Hi-C DNA was mixed with 50 µl of “T4 DNA pol mix” (1x NEBuffer 2.1, 100 µM dATP, 100 µM dGTP, 2.5 U of T4 DNA polymerase (NEB, M0203S)) and incubated for 30 min at 37°C. The sample volumes were brought up to ~130 µl by adding TE buffer. DNA samples were sheared (300–500 bp) using the following settings in Covaris S220 (Duty Factor: 5.0, Peak incident power: 175 W, Cycles per burst: 200, Treatment time: 120 sec) using microTUBE with snap cap (Covaris, 520045). After DNA shearing, DNA size selection was performed using AMPure XP beads (Beckman Coulter). Using the size-selected DNA samples, biotin pull-down and sequencing library preparations were performed using 30 µl of Dynabeads M-280 Streptavidin (Invitrogen, 11206D) and a part of KAPA LTP kit (KAPA BIOSYSTEMS, KK8232) following the kit's protocol. For library amplification, KAPA Real-Time Amplification Kits (KAPA BIOSYSTEMS, KK2701) were used to determine the optimal PCR cycles (5–8 cycles) and the final PCR products were purified by AMPure XP beads.

title: GSM9735858: cPLX018 - GluR1/2+ EV miRNA, PLX5622, Preconditioned Concussion; Mus musculus; miRNA-Seq
protocol: For GluR1/2+ EVs derived from blood serum: We collected blood at 9 days post-injury by administering a lethal dose of sodium pentobarbital (250 mg/kg) and then collecting whole blood via cardiac puncture. We allowed the whole blood to coagulate in uncoated tubes at room temperature for 30-60 minutes and then centrifuged at 433 x g for 15 min at 4C to isolate clear serum. We stored the serum at -80C until processing. We isolated GluR1/2+ EVs from serum using Track Etched NanoPOre (TENPO) devices with 3-um pore-size and immunomagnetic capture. We thawed serum and pooled 1-4 mouse serum samples immediately prior to TENPO processing, excluding serum samples with visible red blood cell contamination. We labeled neuron-enriched EVs by incubating the serum with biotinylated anti-GluR1/2 antibodies. We lysed the GluR1/2+ EVs on chip using QIAzol (Qiagen) to extract the RNA content and isolated miRNAs using miRNeasy kit (Qiagen) and stored the miRNA at -80C until library preparation. For brain nuclei isolation: We administered 250 mg/kg sodium pentobarbital (i.p.) to the mice, quickly removed the brain from the skull, and collected a 1-mm ipsilateral slice of brain tissue directly below the site of injury (-1.5-2 mm from bregma), which was flash-frozen and stored at -80C until nuclei isolation. To isolate nuclei, we first homogenized tissue according to 10X Genomics Demonstrated Protocol CG000214 Rev F: Nuclei Isolation from Cell Suspensions and Tissue for Single Cell RNA Sequencing - Mouse Brain Tissue. We next removed myelin using an iodixanol gradient (Narayanan et al, 2020). Finally, we fixed nuclei using the Evercode Nuclei Fixation v3 Kit (Parse Biosciences) and stored nuclei at -80C until library preparation. For GluR1/2+ EV miRNAs: We used the QIAseq miRNA Library Kit (Qiagen) to produce the miRNA library. We sequenced the library using the NovaSeq 6000 SP Kit (Illumina; Next-Generation Sequencing Core, University of Pennsylvania). For single nucleus RNA: We prepared the library using the Evercode WT v3 Kit (Parse Biosciences), which pools and distributes all 24 samples into 8 sub-libraries. We sequenced using the NovaSeq 6000 SP Kit (Illumina) at Penn's Next Generation Sequencing Core.
